title: Structured Diffusion Bridges: Inductive Bias for Denoising Diffusion Bridges
claim: Our method keeps strong performance as paired supervision shrinks, beating baselines when pairs exist and still working with none.
layout: Single line plot, x paired fraction, y IoU, four colored series
description: A single line chart with paired fraction ρ (0 to 1.0) on the x-axis and IoU (higher is better) on the y-axis, which runs from about 0.45 to 0.80. A legend in the upper left lists LRGT+ (gray), EDM (blue), LDDBM (orange) and SDB (ours, green). The green SDB line is the only one that starts at ρ=0, at about 0.55. It rises to about 0.64 at ρ=0.5 and about 0.68 at ρ=1.0. EDM and LDDBM start only at ρ=0.5, at about 0.47 and 0.51. They climb steeply to about 0.63 and 0.66 at ρ=1.0, so the gap to SDB narrows as pairing increases. The gray LRGT+ reference line sits highest, at about 0.70 and 0.76. Markers have small error bars, and there is a light grid. The eye goes first to the green line, which has the longest span.
caption: Multi-view →3D (ShapeNet). Reconstruction fidelity (IoU) versus paired fraction ρ when translating four-view images into 323 voxel grids. SDB (ours) outperforms diffusion-bridge baselines (EDM (Karras et al., 2022), LDDBM (Berman et al., 2026)) whenever paired supervision is available (ρ ∈{0.5, 1.0}), while remaining applicable in the fully unpaired setting (ρ = 0) where paired objectives cannot be trained. LRGT+ (Yang et al., 2023) is an ad-hoc pipeline included as a reference point rather than a principled diffusion-bridge baseline.
abstract: Modality translation is inherently under-constrained, as multiple cross-modal mappings may yield the same marginals. Recent work has shown that diffusion bridges are effective for this task. However, most existing approaches rely on fully paired datasets, thereby imposing a single data-driven constraint. We propose a diffusion-bridge framework that characterizes the space of admissible solutions and restricts it via alignment constraints, treating paired supervision as an optional heuristic rather than a prerequisite. We validate our method on synthetic and real modality translation benchmarks across unpaired, semi-paired, and paired regimes, showing consistent performance across supervision levels. Notably, \textbf{it achieves near fully-paired quality with a substantial relaxation in pairing requirements, and remaining applicable in the unpaired regime}. These results highlight diffusion bridges as a flexible foundation for modality translation beyond fully paired data.
